title: The Math to Quit Your Job Without Selling Stocks

beats.say: Your $50,000 paycheck. That’s $4,166 a month after taxes.
beats.visual: A paycheck envelope on a wooden desk, soft side lighting, slight tilt

beats.say: To replace it with passive income, how much do you actually need?
beats.visual: Close-up of a calculator screen showing $4,166, shallow depth of field

beats.say: Most people think they need $1,200,000 in cash. That’s the 4% rule talking.
beats.visual: A stack of cash on a table, side angle, warm lighting

beats.say: But if you own assets that pay you directly, the math shifts.
beats.visual: A row of rental property mailboxes with keys, dusk light

beats.say: A 6% net yield portfolio throwing off $4,166 a month needs just $833,200.
beats.visual: Humming server racks in a data center, cool blue light

beats.say: At 8%, it’s $624,900. At 10%, it’s $499,920. Same income, smaller pile.
beats.visual: Dividend check on a kitchen table, neutral light

beats.say: So why does everyone chase the bigger number?
beats.visual: A city skyline with a single illuminated office window, night

beats.say: Because most assets don’t pay out that cleanly. Tenants vanish. Dividends get cut.
beats.visual: A vacated apartment door with a ‘For Rent’ sign, muted tones

beats.say: The real catch: you need assets that pay on time, every time, no excuses.
beats.visual: A clock tower at 12:00 with sunlight hitting the face

beats.say: Start small. This week, list one asset class you can own that pays monthly.
beats.visual: A notebook with a pen resting on a blank page, soft light

beats.say: Then crunch the yield. $4,166 divided by your target portfolio size. That’s your number.
beats.visual: A calculator with a hand pressing the equals button, close-up

beats.say: The paycheck replacement equation: net yield beats portfolio size. Follow for the money rules school never taught you.
beats.visual: A quiet street at dawn with a single lit streetlamp

caption: You don’t need a mountain of cash to quit. You need the right yield. Math inside.
description: Replacing a $50,000 paycheck isn’t about the pile—it’s about the payout. Here’s the net yield math to walk away from your job without selling assets.
first_comment: What’s one asset you’d add to this list?

facts.claim: A 6% net yield portfolio requires $833,200 to generate $4,166/month ($50,000/year pre-tax).
A 4% withdrawal rate requires $1,200,000 to generate $50,000/year.
facts.basis: 4% rule guideline from the 1998 Trinity study

facts.claim: At 8% annual return, investing $1,000/month reaches $600,000 in 20.2 years.

loop_map.big_question: How much do you need to replace it with passive income?
